walkthroughs.body_html:
Group 1: down the group, easier to lose outer electron.

Group 7: down the group, harder to gain outer electron.

Li - crimson, Na - yellow, K - lilac.

Ca - orange-red, Cu - green-blue.

Chloride: AgCl white.

Bromide: AgBr cream. Iodide: AgI yellow.

Sulfate: BaSO4 white. Carbonate: CO2 cloudy limewater.

mcqs.q: Why does first ionisation energy generally increase across a period?
options: Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
Atoms get bigger across a period, making electrons easier to add but harder to remove.
Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays roughly constant, so electrons are held more tightly.
A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
Delocalised electrons are free to move through the lattice of positive ions, carrying charge.
Metal atoms themselves move to carry the current.
Metals contain naturally moving protons that act as charge carriers.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a strong acid and a concentrated acid?
options: Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
Strong and concentrated mean the same thing for acids.
A strong acid fully dissociates in water; a concentrated acid has a high amount of acid per volume — these are independent properties.
